clue.text: Virginia's mother, at the tea table, fumes

parts.note: VA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
at a tea table it is traditionally mother who pours out the tea

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia watches her mother seethe while serving tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia looks like a woman's name but is the US state, VA. 'Who'll be mother?' is the British tea-table phrase for who will pour.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapours are exhalations or gases, the same thing as smoky fumes rising off something.

clue.text: Sharp dressers use it:!

parts.note: sharp means sour-tasting and dressers are people dressing a salad, not smart clothes-wearers

explanation.surface: Stylish people rely on some fashion secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad dressing is commonly made with this sour liquid, which tastes sharp.

clue.text: Quite uncorrupted Pole is in the bag

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, sitting in it

parts.note: pure means entirely free of corruption
S stands for South, one of the Earth's poles

explanation.surface: An honest Polish man's success is assured, in the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; here it is the South Pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is a small bag for carrying money.

clue.text: Might be Svetlana's marriage to James Bond!

definitions.text: Might be Svetlana's marriage to James Bond!

parts.words: Might be Svetlana's marriage to James Bond
parts.note: a Russian Svetlana belongs to the Soviet one, a marriage is one, and a bond is one too

explanation.surface: A Russian woman named Svetlana might wed the fictional spy 007.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a wedding, a joining of things, and a federation such as the Soviet one.

clue.text: Sir must order an Egyptian instrument

indicators.note: to order letters is to arrange them afresh, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight is required to commission an ancient Egyptian musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sistrum is a rattle with metal discs played in ancient Egyptian worship.

clue.text: Not Mrs T's turn to run round the tree, but she's high in public esteem!

indicators.note: the tree's letters run around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a poplar is a tall tree
Mrs Thatcher famously said she was not for turning, so the turn she refused was a U-turn, giving U

explanation.surface: Mrs Thatcher would not make a U-turn round the tree, yet she was well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs T is Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister whose line 'The lady's not for turning' rejected a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone popular is well liked, held in high regard by the public.

clue.text: It's behind the castle gate

parts.note: the item sought is the castle gate at the back, not something lying behind it

explanation.surface: Something is concealed behind a castle's gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a rear or side entrance in a castle wall.

clue.text: He wears blue cuffs to help him keep the peace

definitions.text: He wears blue cuffs to help him keep the peace

parts.words: He wears blue cuffs to help him keep the peace
parts.note: blue is the uniform colour and cuffs are handcuffs, not shirt cuffs

explanation.surface: A man in blue-cuffed shirts tries to keep everyone calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer wears a blue uniform and uses handcuffs while maintaining public order.

clue.text: One who has grounds to prosecute trespassers

definitions.text: One who has grounds to prosecute trespassers

parts.words: One who has grounds to prosecute trespassers
parts.note: grounds means estate land, not legal justification

explanation.surface: A person with good legal reason to sue intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: A property holder owns the land on which trespassers intrude.

clue.text: People have to read them for hours!

definitions.text: People have to read them for hours

parts.words: People have to read them for hours
parts.note: the hours are working shifts listed on a duty sheet, not long spells of reading

explanation.surface: Some books are so long people read them for hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty lists show workers which shifts or hours they must work.

clue.text: Good looking lad, but made a bloomer

definitions.meaning: the handsome youth of Greek myth who loved his own reflection
he was turned into a flower, the plant also bearing this name

explanation.surface: A handsome boy nevertheless made a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is slang for a mistake; here it is literally a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the beautiful youth pined at his reflection and became the daffodil-like flower.

clue.text: Dry cleaners work on them

parts.note: read as clothes that have been cleaned, hung out to dry on ropes, not a dry-cleaning shop

explanation.surface: Dry-cleaning staff handle certain items.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing is hung on clothes lines in the open air to dry.

clue.text: One carelessly reaping the benefit for him

definitions.text: One carelessly reaping the benefit for him

parts.words: One carelessly reaping the benefit for him
parts.note: the harvesters reap carelessly, and the leftovers benefit the person gathering after them

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtlessly profits from another's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers grain left behind in the field after reapers have passed.

clue.text: Put with your letter instruction to surround the place

definitions.meaning: the word written on a note telling you to include an item in the envelope
to shut a place in on all sides, as with a fence

explanation.surface: Instructions to post something with a letter and to cordon off a site.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in with a letter, or to fence an area in, both mean to shut it within.

clue.text: Dan mourns murdered employee of the baker, perhaps

indicators.note: murdered suggests the letters are mangled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan grieves for a baker's worker who was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundsman delivers goods on a regular route, such as bread for a baker.

clue.text: It must be the same word for it

definitions.text: It must be the same word for it

parts.words: It must be the same word for it
parts.note: the clue describes something kept just as it was, which is also what the word itself means

explanation.surface: A remark that one expression must stay identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unchanged remains exactly the same as before.

clue.text: The French coach industry

definitions.meaning: a public stagecoach formerly used in France

explanation.surface: A French sports trainer works in manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: Industry suggests manufacturing but here means hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means painstaking effort and was also the name of the old French stagecoach.

clue.text: Arithmetical symbol for nothing, no less!

definitions.text: Arithmetical symbol for nothing, no less!

parts.words: Arithmetical symbol for nothing, no less
parts.note: the symbol is the subtraction sign, which also reads as the word less

explanation.surface: A sum's sign meaning nothing at all, would you believe.
explanation.definitionFit: The subtraction sign is a short horizontal stroke meaning take away, or less.

clue.text: Holding arms? Have a word with them both. Make it short

definitions.text: Holding arms? Have a word with them both. Make it short

parts.words: Holding arms? Have a word with them both. Make it short
parts.note: the word goes before arms and before talk-like phrases: pistols are this kind of arms, and short means little

explanation.surface: Someone holding weapons is told to have a brief chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Small means little or short, and small arms are handguns and rifles.

clue.text: One is aware it means the opposite

definitions.text: One is aware it means the opposite

parts.words: One is aware it means the opposite
parts.note: aware stands for awake, and this word means the opposite of being awake

explanation.surface: Someone knows a word has the reverse meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is sleep, the state opposite to being awake and aware.

clue.text: Prod melon about to ensure it's sweet

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poke a melon to check that it is ripe and sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: This boiled sweet is a lemon-flavoured candy.

clue.text: Shut up without a key?

parts.note: shut up means closed fast, held by a catch that needs no key, not told to be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone locked in with no key to get out.
explanation.definitionFit: A door fastened with a catch is closed securely without needing a key.

clue.text: Learned man is one dead dog!

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a scholarly degree
a stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: A scholar is a dead dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Used by advertisers who send off mail

definitions.meaning: large printed notices pasted up to advertise

explanation.surface: Advertisers rely on people who mail things out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both printed bills for display and those who put letters in the post.

clue.text: Has risen, drunk and tense

parts.note: someone who has risen out of bed is up
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone got up, got drunk and became anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means nervously tense and anxious.

clue.text: Place to eat in the vessel for horses

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: SS is steamship, a vessel
a table is where meals are eaten

explanation.surface: A dining spot aboard a ship carrying horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the slightly loose 'for horses', meaning the buildings that are for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stables are buildings provided to house horses.

clue.text: But one doesn't get a lighter sentence for it!

definitions.text: But one doesn't get a lighter sentence for it!

parts.words: But one doesn't get a lighter sentence for it
parts.note: lighter suggests a lenient sentence but refers to a fire-starting device

explanation.surface: A crime that earns no leniency in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Free to be immoral!

definitions.meaning: immoral means of lax morals, dissolute

explanation.surface: Liberty to behave badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unfastened and morally lax.

clue.text: Farm building with nothing in it but a bit of beef

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the farm building

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty barn holding only some beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron of beef is a large joint of two sirloins joined at the backbone.

clue.text: May drop the temperature below zero

definitions.text: May drop the temperature below zero

parts.words: May drop the temperature below zero
parts.note: drop means fall from the sky, and the object is frozen, formed below zero

explanation.surface: Weather in May might fall below freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice that falls from clouds when the air is below freezing.

clue.text: Ginger nut!

parts.note: ginger hair is red
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A gingernut biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A gingernut is a British spiced biscuit; read instead as a ginger-haired head.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with red hair is described as ginger-haired.

clue.text: Containers on fire — protect the car!

definitions.meaning: low metal frames round a fireplace keeping coals in
car guards over the wheels, also bumpers

explanation.surface: Burning containers, and a warning to shield the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both fireplace guards and protective panels on a vehicle.
